key_insight: Integrating economic analysis with AI design and policy can align incentives, quantify social value, and guide deployment decisions so AI systems contribute measurably to the common good rather than only private profit.
problem_solved: Addresses market failures and misaligned incentives that cause AI deployments to produce negative externalities, unequal benefits, and underinvestment in public-interest capabilities.
method: Proposes an economic framework that maps incentives, costs, benefits, and externalities across stakeholders to evaluate AI outcomes for the public good.
Defines measurable social-value metrics and trade-off criteria to compare alternative AI designs, pricing models, and governance interventions.
Applies conceptual analysis and illustrative case studies to show how policy tools (subsidies, regulation, public procurement) and design choices change incentive structures.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and policymakers practical tools to assess social value, redesign incentives, and choose deployment strategies that maximize public benefits while minimizing harms.
visual_elements: Stakeholder-incentive diagram showing flows of costs, benefits, and externalities between users, firms, and society
Cost–benefit heatmap comparing private profit vs. social value across AI use cases
Decision flowchart linking design choices and policy tools to expected social outcomes
Metric dashboard mockup displaying proposed social-value indicators (equity, accessibility, public-good contribution)
paper_title: AI economics for the common good
